draft.title: Decentralisation
card: Decentralisation means spreading people and jobs away from the biggest cities to regional centres. A regional centre is a town or smaller city outside the big capitals.
Governments may try it by moving government offices, building roads and rail, or offering support to businesses that set up in the regions.
The aim can be to ease crowding and pressure on housing and transport in big cities, and to give regional areas more people, jobs and services.
Canberra was planned partly with this aim. It was built inland as the national capital, so the national government would be based away from the large coastal cities.
draft.remember: Decentralisation moves people and jobs from big cities to regional centres.

a.q: Which action is an example of decentralisation?
opts: Moving a government office from Brisbane to a regional town
Building more apartment towers in the centre of Brisbane
Adding new train lines inside Brisbane's busy suburbs
Opening a new shopping centre on the edge of Brisbane
a.why: Moving an office to a regional town shifts jobs away from a big city to a regional centre. Building more housing in the city centre does the opposite, as it keeps people and activity in the big city.
a.clue: Look for the option that moves jobs out of the big city.

b.q: Why is Canberra described as planned partly with decentralisation in mind?
opts: It put the national capital inland, away from big coastal cities
It was built to be the largest port city in Australia
It was designed to hold most of Australia's people
It was set up to be the main place that exports leave from
b.why: Canberra was built inland as the national capital, so national government activity was based away from the large coastal cities. It was not meant to be a port or the biggest city, as those ideas would add to concentration on the coast.
b.clue: Think about where Canberra sits compared with the large capitals.
